summary: Return-path asymmetry via Internet Gateway causes TLS session stickiness and selective 401s for presigned artifact downloads
description: Issue summary: FinSight reports intermittent 401 Unauthorized when downloading large presigned S3 artifacts from serving nodes in their private deployment. Failures are selective (only a small fraction of requests) and correlate with longer-lived gRPC streams and model pulls. Impact: Customer reports degraded model initialization times and occasional inference failures impacting production traffic for a critical analytics pipeline. Environment: Private deployment (VPC peering to Redwood control plane), prod/us-east. Observed behavior: - ~0.5-2% of presigned GETs return 401 from our artifact CDN for nodes behind customer's egress path. - Affected requests show valid presigned URL (works if retried immediately to a different node). - When 401 occurs, subsequent retries often succeed for same user after short delay. Steps to reproduce: 1) From a serving node in customer's VPC, request a large model artifact presigned URL and start streaming the download. 2) Simultaneously generate high-volume outbound requests (egress) that cause the node's return path to resolve via customer's Internet Gateway (IGW) for a subset of flows. 3) Observe selective 401s on presigned GETs. Expected behavior: Presigned artifact fetches should succeed consistently regardless of egress return path; auth should validate the signed URL and not depend on source path. Additional context: This deployment uses a transit route table that propagates a default route via a TGW to a partner network; however, some return-path traffic for ephemeral ports is routed to the IGW due to asymmetric route propagation and NAT behavior on the customer side.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:20 - Support intake: Customer provided VPC flow logs and a small pcap. 2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE collected tcpdump on serving node during reproduction; observed SYN/SYN-ACK then data, but TLS sessions sometimes resumed on a different 5-tuple. 2026-03-10 11:30 - Correlation: 401s aligned with source IP change in connection logs; presigned auth backend occasionally saw a different source IP for the same request (bounced via IGW), which invalidated an IP-based short-term binding in a cached auth layer. 2026-03-10 14:00 - Route analysis: customer's route tables show TGW -> spoke propagation for most prefixes, but ephemeral-source-specific policy-based NAT at on-prem edge causes replies for ephemeral ports > 32768 to egress via IGW. 2026-03-11 09:00 - Control-plane logs: auth service applied a temporary anti-replay heuristic that expected stable source IP during request lifetime; heuristic flagged requests with mid-request source change and returned 401. 2026-03-11 13:15 - Hypothesis: Asymmetric return path (request enters via peering/TGW but return takes IGW with rewritten source IP) causes auth layer to see inconsistent source and reject presigned tokens that had optional source-binding set. 2026-03-12 08:40 - Reproduced in lab by injecting asymmetric return route; reproduced 401 pattern when source IP changed mid-stream.
comments: Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports intermittent 401s since 2026-03-09 late afternoon. Provided flow logs and sample request IDs.

Luca Rossi (SRE): Captured tcpdump and confirmed mid-request source IP change. Hypothesis: asymmetric return path + edge NAT causes auth source-binding mismatch. Opened infra PR to make auth fallback tolerant for presigned artifacts (see related_github_prs).
Customer (FinSight - Rajiv Patel): We're observing impacts on model boot times; can you propose a short-term mitigation?
workaround: Short-term: Disable source-IP binding option on presigned URLs for this customer (permitted by policy) and increase auth token grace window to 30s. This avoids rejecting mid-stream source changes while a long-term fix is implemented.
resolution: In progress - temporary mitigation deployed 2026-03-11: source-IP binding disabled for FinSight and auth service updated to allow one mid-request source shift for presigned artifact flows. Long-term plan: coordinate with customer to fix asymmetric routing (update TGW propagation and NAT policy) and harden auth cache to validate on signature rather than source IP. Follow-up task created to track TGW/routing changes and to add a feature flag for source-binding strictness.
next_steps: 1) Schedule joint network review with FinSight networking team to correct return-path asymmetry (owner: FinSight). 2) Engineering to land PR to remove source-IP as required auth factor for presigned artifact validation (owner: infra team, PR in progress). 3) Monitor artifact 401 rate for 48 hours post-mitigation and revert change if no issues.
resolution_notes: Mitigation reduced 401 rate from ~1.8% to ~0.02% in initial 24h window. No new regressions observed in control-plane auth metrics. Customer confirmed improved model boot reliability on 2026-03-12.
